verdict.rationale: Make documents a public REST API and an official MCP server that lets AI clients "view and modify scenarios" and "manage the contents of your Make account", so an agent can programmatically modify workflows. However, the evidence never shows scenario-specific create, update, or activate endpoints in the public REST API. The AI Agents CRUD endpoints [make-docs-37] cover a different entity and are not credited here. Missing for 10: documented scenario create/update endpoints in the public API, an explicit activate/deactivate scenario operation, and hands-on or independent corroboration of an agent doing this end-to-end.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent create, update, and activate a workflow programmatically through the public API

citations.quote: View and modify scenarios and their related entities (e.g., connections, webhooks, and data stores)
Make MCP server allows AI systems, such as large language models (LLMs), to run scenarios and manage the contents of your Make account.
The Make API follows the REST API design. Make API is organized into resource-oriented URLs
